title: Remove automated database backups
context: Cost optimization sprint — infra spend was 40% over budget. Team proposed cutting nightly backup jobs to save cloud storage costs.
reasoning: Backups were deemed redundant because we had point-in-time recovery enabled on the primary DB. The team estimated $2,400/month savings with minimal risk given recent stability.
assumptions: Point-in-time recovery covers all failure scenarios
No schema migrations planned for 90 days
outcome: Six weeks later, a bad migration corrupted production data. Recovery took 18 hours. Customer-facing SLA breach and emergency postmortem.

title: Use vector-only RAG for agent memory
context: Building v1 of an autonomous support agent. Needed fast retrieval over 50k support tickets.
reasoning: Pure vector search is simpler to ship, well-understood by the team, and benchmarks showed acceptable recall@5 on ticket similarity.
assumptions: Similarity equals relevance for support queries
Outcome quality does not need to influence retrieval
Static embeddings are sufficient for evolving policies
outcome: Agent frequently retrieved outdated resolutions with high similarity scores. Escalation rate increased 22% over two sprints.
evidence: Audit log: 34% of retrieved chunks flagged outdated by support leads

title: Adopt Hindsight for decision memory
context: After two failed memory approaches, team evaluated outcome-aware memory systems for the support agent.
reasoning: Hindsight retain/recall/reflect model weights memories by outcomes, supports premise drift detection, and provides an auditable decision ledger.
assumptions: Outcome signals can be captured at decision time
Engineering team will annotate decisions consistently
Hindsight server latency fits our p95 budget
outcome: Escalation rate dropped 18% within one sprint. Audit view surfaced three stale-retrieval bugs that were fixed via outcome_weight_floor tuning.
evidence: Audit log: outcome_weight_floor tuned from 0.1 to 0.35

title: Defer agent observability to Phase 2
context: MVP deadline in 3 weeks. OpenTelemetry integration estimated at 5 engineer-days.
reasoning: Ship core agent loop first; add tracing once usage patterns are understood. Logging to stdout deemed sufficient for launch.
assumptions: Stdout logs are enough to debug early failures
No production traffic in first 30 days
outcome: First production incident took 6 hours to diagnose with log grep alone. Phase 2 observability work was pulled forward under fire.
evidence: Sprint retro: observability bumped to P0
